name: Marraco
body:
Marraco
CR 8

This spiny, wingless reptile has an enormous mouth split into gruesome quadrate jaws, with a toothy maw large enough for a human to stand in and tongues of flame licking out past its massive fangs.

XP 4,800
N Huge dragon (fire)
Init -1; Senses darkvision 120 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +12

DEFENSE

AC 23, touch 7, flat-footed 23 (-1 Dex, +16 natural, –2 size)
hp 94 (9d12+45)
Fort 10, Ref 5, Will 8
DR 5/magic; Immune fire, paralysis, sleep

OFFENSE

Speed 50 ft.
Melee bite +15 (2d6+12/19-20 plus grab), 2 claws +10 (1d8+4)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 10 ft. (15 ft. with bite)
Special Attacks breath weapon (30-ft. cone, DC 18, 10d6 fire, usable every 1d4 rounds), fast swallow, swallow whole (2d6 bludgeoning and 2d6 fire, AC 18, 9 hp)

STATISTICS

Str 27, Dex 9, Con 18, Int 5, Wis 11, Cha 9
Base Atk +9; CMB +19 (+23 to grapple); CMD 28 (+32 vs trip)
Feats Improved Critical (bite), Iron Will, Power Attack, Toughness, Vital Strike
Skills Climb +20, Perception +12, Stealth +11
Languages Draconic
SQ woodland stride

ECOLOGY

Environment any hill and forest
Organization solitary
Treasure double

These lesser cousins of true dragons prefer hilly, forested regions. Unable to fly like their greater kin, the marraco stalks its prey on foot, willing and able to track a scent for days. Marraco are voracious and greedy eaters, swallowing their prey mostly whole, up to and including horses and elk.

An adult marraco averages 32 feet in length from the tip of its snout to its thick, short tail. Its heavy scales are mottled purplish gray on its top and sides, darkening to a muddy brown on its underside. A row of black spines crests the dragon’s head, running the length of its back and tail.

The marraco can breathe fire, though not with the heat and intensity of a red dragon. A marraco is cunning enough to use its fire breath in hunting, sometimes setting brush aflame to scare potential prey into the open. Some marraco appear to prefer cooked meat and scorches prey with their flame breath before gulping down the corpse.
